title: SC11 scope-tuple (CM-54 typed-scope-partition)
description: SC11 declares TWO distinct named scope objects, because Round 2 adjudicated two different triples and Wave 1 must not overload one key with two meanings. (1) `scope` = {workspace, project, layer} -- 05-DATA-MODEL.md line 174, the typed triple behind the promotion tree; `layer` is what makes Project Rule and Global Rule two different terminal states (06-PROMOTION-POLICY). This root schema IS that object. (2) `cohort` = {workspace, project, path} -- 05-DATA-MODEL.md line 177 invariant 4 ('Typed 3-tuple identity (workspace_id, project_id, path) on every domain row'), which is exactly the key set the FROZEN kernel reads: kd_provenance.cohort_key(scope) consumes workspace, project and path and nothing else (scripts/kd_provenance.py lines 55-63), and is_independent / independent_support read rec['cohort'] (lines 136, 152). `path` was REMOVED from this root object: it belongs to `cohort` only. `layer` never belongs to `cohort` -- the kernel ignores it there, which is how the pre-split overload stayed invisible. Hard constraints still apply to `scope`: S1 non-empty and fail-closed, never defaulted to global (line 176); S2 a scope column with zero read points is rejected (lines 178-181) -- S04 kd_scope_resolve proves the read points and reports `layer` as PENDING_CONSUMER until Wave 3's S10 lands. The kernel function and its key names are not renamed or edited: S19's mutation gate depends on them.

workspace.description: 05 §5.3 S1 (line 176). First component of BOTH objects: scope.workspace and cohort.workspace must hold the same value, and S04 refuses a line where they disagree.

project.description: 05 §5.3 S1 (line 176). Second component of both objects; missing it makes counts global, the exact `02` defect DD-6 lists as a reopen condition (DEFERRED id DD-6-sub44 -- still deferred, not decided here).

layer.description: 05 §5.3 line 174: `layer ∈ {project, global, cohort}`. Enum is exactly the adjudicated set. S1 (line 176) forbids defaulting a missing layer to `global`. Wave 1 readers: S05 kd_identity_key (identity field) and the SC02/SC03 rows. Wave 1 has NO promotion-tree reader: S10 arrives in Wave 3, so S04 reports this field PENDING_CONSUMER and, under the stricter exit-code branch, exits 2 until that reader exists. IMPLEMENTATION_GAP: Round 2 never decided whether PENDING_CONSUMER is exit 0 or exit 2 / DEFERRED id unknown (nearest DD-6-sub44, left deferred).

scope_resolution_line.description: One line of S04 `scope.jsonl`. `resolution` distinguishes an adopted triple from a fail-closed rejection so that 'never resolved' is never rendered as a real scope (05 §5.4 admission rule (3), line 199: templates must tell 'never measured' apart from '0').

scope.description: The SC11 typed triple, present only when resolution == 'resolved' (05 §5.3 S1: reject, do not fabricate a scope).

cohort.description: The kernel identity triple for the same line (05 line 177). Present only when resolution == 'resolved'.

cohort_key.description: Proof of consumption, not a second authority: the value returned by kd_provenance.cohort_key for this cohort. S04 exists to make the 'computed but unconsumed' defect detectable (05 §5.3 S2), so S04 calls the kernel function itself.

cohort_triple.title: identity cohort triple (05-DATA-MODEL.md line 177 invariant 4)
cohort_triple.description: The typed 3-tuple identity on every domain row, under the field NAME the frozen kernel reads (`rec['cohort']`, kd_provenance.py lines 55-63, 136, 152). Support counting groups by this object: two events in one cohort with different `path` are two cohorts. `layer` is NOT a member -- putting it here was the Wave 1 overload this split removes. `path` may be the empty string, which means 'whole project' and is an OBSERVED value; a missing key is a partial scope and is refused (fail-closed, invariant 4).

workspace.description: Same value as scope.workspace; S04 rejects a mismatch.

path.description: Third identity coordinate read by kd_provenance.cohort_key (kernel line 62). Key must be present; "" means whole-project, an absent key means unobserved and is rejected.
